questions.solution_html:
• How can a process execute its critical section? [U] / [CO3]
  • When one process is executing in its critical section, no other process is allowed to execute in its critical
  • section. Each process must request permission to enter its critical section. The section of code
  • implementing this request is the entry section, exit section and the remainder section.

questions.question: Differentiate Microkernels and Module based operating system structures. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate Microkernels and Module based operating system structures. [U] / [CO1]
  • Micro Kernel, contains a minimum number of functions that are required, data, and features
  • simply to implement OS. Features of Microkernel include Minimalist design. High flexibility,
  • Reliable and Portable - (3 marks)
  • Modular Kernel, is a type of kernel in which some parts of the system core will get allocated
  • in independent files called modules. This can be added to the system at run time. It usually
  • requires a small amount of time to load modules. Its features include:
  • Monolithic design, Low flexibility, Efficient: and Performance-oriented. -- (3 marks)

questions.question: Discuss Dual Mode operation in operating system. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss dual mode operation in operating system. [U] / [CO1]
  • Dual mode operation is a mec hanism that allows an operating system to protect system
  • resources by running programs in two different modes:
  • • User Mode: Used for executing application programs. Has restricted access to
  • hardware and system resources. Cannot execute privileged instructions.
  • • Kernel Mode (Supervisor Mode): Used by the operating system.
  • • Mode Bit: A special hardware bit indicates the current mode (user = 0,
  • Kernel = 1).Ensures the system knows which mode is active.
  • Explanation with figure give full marks.

questions.solution_html:
• Compare and contrast paging and segmentation in detail. [An] / [CO4]
  • Paging is a memory management technique in which process address space is broken into blocks of
  • the same size called pages (size is power of 2, between 512 bytes and 8192 bytes). Similarly, main
  • memory is divided into small fixed-sized blocks of (physical) memory called frames and the size of a
  • frame is kept the same as that of a page to have optimum.
  • Segmentation is a memory-management scheme that supports this programmer view of
  • Memory.
  • Explanation paging and Paging Hardware with TLB and diagram -7 marks
  • Explanation of segmentation with Segmentation Hardware and diagram – 6 marks.
  • Comparison of paging and segmentation – 2marks
